informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.swa: One of the most unique species of primate, Allen's Swamp Monkey are actually swimmers! Their unique adaptation of webbed feet attribute towards their name, and they are primarily found in the swamps of Southern Africa. Despite this unique adaptation, the 40+ sized troops of Swamp Monkey primarily inhabit the trees and treetops of the rainforest. Like many other primate species, the swamp monkey practices social grooming, strengthening troop bonds by grooming each other.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.wil: Blue Wildebeest are one of 2 species of Wildebeest found on the African Savannah. The primary difference between the 2 species is physical appearance, they are generally larger in size and their tails are thinner and darker than the Black Wildebeest's recognisable white hair. These medium sized antelopes partake in one of the greatest  migrations on Earth, travelling 1000s of miles over plains, rivers, and sometimes certain lions pushed off cliffs by their adoptive brothers, in search of the rains.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.pro: Not only do Pronghorns have the longest land migration in North America, they are also the fastest land animal in North America. Pronghorn can run  at speeds close to 60 miles an hour, and have the ability to maintain it for a decent amount of time. Interestingly, Pronghorn are abundant in North America, so much so that populations are too high for the ecosystems! Currently, there are plans to repopulate the National Parks of which they live with predators so that the population can return to a balanced level.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.ger: The most notable characteristics of the Gerenuk, also known as the 'giraffe gazelle', are its long, slender neck, thin legs and short snout. These distinguish it from other antelopes and make it easier to identify. On the whole, they are similar to most other african hoofstock behaviourally, however they can actually stand up to get to their food! The Gerenuk's diet consists of plant matter from trees and bushes, and the unique structures in their spine allow them to stand upright on their hind legs, to reach as high as 2m in the air!
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.pot: With its round head, small ears & massive golden brown eyes, The Potto is one of the most unusual looking species on the planet. They are a primitive primate species, also known as a Prosimian, and are known for their strong scent, described as smelling like curry! Pottos are actually nocturnal animals, therefore keeping these animals in captivity may be difficult. Additionally,  Pottos are uniquely adapted with strong jaws, to enable them to eat lumps of dried gum that are usually too tough for other tree dwellers.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.hyr: Hyrax are basically your standard, average rodent - you would think. However, these guinea-pig imposters are both arboreal and loud, preferring to live at high elevations and are well known for their awful screams. It should also be recognised that despite their tiny size, they are the closest loving relative of the Elephant - the largest land mammal on the planet, even if they are 1/2250th the weight of their pachyderm cousins. These rodents are gradually becoming more common in captivity and luckily, their wild population is stable.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.lan: Langurs are a group of Old World Monkeys, recognised for their elongated bodies, extended tails and remarkable facial features. This peculiar primate is primarily tree-dwelling and spends much of its life in the canopy. Langurs are also notable for their intricate social structures, unique means of communication and crucial role in their environment! However, Langurs are unfortunately on the whole extremely endangered, and threatened with poaching & habitat loss - one species was actually thought extinct until 2012.

The François' langur, also known as the Francois' leaf monkey, Tonkin leaf monkey, or white side-burned black langur is a species of langur exhibiting black, silky hair and very distinct white sideburns that grow down from their ears to the corners of their cheeks. François' langurs are diurnal and social creatures that spend most of the day resting and foraging, with the average group size ranges from 4 to 27. These monkeys live in a matriarchal society where the females lead the group.

Hanuman Langurs, also known as Northern plains gray langurs, are a species of langur native to Asia. Interestingly, they are a species both terrestrial and arboreal, spending about equal time on the ground as in the trees. They are social animals and can live in several different types of groups: Groups of multiple males and females, one male and multiple females, or multiple males with no females. Males can also live alone without a group. Group sizes can exceed 100 individuals.

The dusky leaf monkey, dusky langur, or spectacled leaf monkey is a species of langur found in Malaysia, Myanmar and Thailand, and occasionally Singapore. They are notable due to their exhibiting large, white colored patches, surrounding its eyes which look like sporting eyeglasses! According to the IUCN, the dusky leaf monkey's population is declining due to habitat loss, poaching, and anthropogenic land use.

The purple-faced langur, also known as the purple-faced leaf monkey, is a species of Old World monkey endemic to Sri Lanka. The animal is a long-tailed arboreal species, identified by a mostly brown appearance, dark face and very shy nature. The species was once highly prevalent, found in suburban Colombo and the "wet zone" villages, but rapid urbanization has led to a significant decrease in their population level.

The East Javan langur is a species of Old World monkey native to the island of Java. The Latin word auratus in its scientific name means "golden", and refers to a less common color variant (In Exhibit Additions, the rarer golden colouration is assigned to the East Javan Langur). The Javan langur has a specialised stomach to digest plant material more efficiently and also has enlarged salivary glands to assist it in breaking down food.

Until recently, West Javan langurs were considered to be a subspecies of the Javan langur, until a 2008 phylogenetic study found that they were deserving of their own species designation. This taxonomical change was adopted by the IUCN in late 2020. Because this change was only recently widely adopted, most research about Javan langurs lumps West Javan and East Javan langurs together as one species. (In Exhibit Additions, the West Javan Langur is represented by the more common Black colour morph).

The leucistic langur, specifically the leucistic white langur, is a rare population of langurs found near Sri Lanka’s Sinharaja Forest Reserve. These langurs exhibit a partial loss of pigmentation, which is distinct from albinism, where there is a complete absence of melanin. Researchers have documented around 30 white langurs in the area, which has transformed Lankagama into an ecotourism hub, benefiting the local community and conservation efforts.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.pec: Peccaries are medium sized, even toed ungulates found in South & Central America. On the whole, peccaries are actually pretty similar to their domesticated cousins, however there is one key difference. Peccaries are actually extremely aggressive and have been known to cause a great deal of damage to humans, so much so that one species is known as the 'javelina', the spanish word for javelin, due to their razor sharp tusks! Despite this, peccaries are actually omnivorous and are not seen as predators, despite their tendency to attack.

The white-lipped peccary is a species of peccary found in Central and South America and the only member of the genus Tayassu. White-lipped peccaries are similar in appearance to pigs, but covered in dark hair (except on certain regions, such as the throat, where it is cream, hence their name). Their range, which extends from Mexico to Argentina, has become fragmented, and the species' population is declining overall. As social animals, white-lipped peccaries typically forage in large groups, which can have as many as 300 peccaries.

The Chacoan peccary is a large mammal with a pig-like appearance. This unique animal is the largest peccary species, from which it differs in a number of ways  - for example exhibiting 3 toes on its hind feet, where other peccaries possess only 2. It is believed to be the closest living relative to the extinct genus Platygonus. This species was described in the 1930s, based on sub-fossil - The Chacoan peccary was classified as a separate species only in 1975, becoming one of the most recently discovered large mammal species.

The Collared peccary, commonly referred to as javelina, saíno, or báquiro, is native to a rather large area - stretching from South America to Central America and as far north as the southern portions of Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas in the U.S. They are also found in habitats shared by humans, merely requiring sufficient cover,  e.g. cities, suburbs and agricultural land throughout their range. Although Collared peccaries seem to be helpless, in fact, they can defend themselves against the most fearsome predators, using their hordes.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.kli: The klipspringer is a small, sturdy antelope first described by German zoologist Eberhard August Wilhelm von Zimmermann in 1783. A gregarious animal, the klipspringer forms lifelong pair bonds and mates stay as close as within 5m of each other at most times. The Klipspringer is uniquely adapted to its surroundings - it walks on the tips of its cylindrical, blunt hooves. This enhances the grip on the ground, enabling the animal to deftly climb and jump over rocky surfaces.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.wal: Wallabies are a diverse group of marsupials found primarily in Australia and New Guinea. They are known for their powerful hind legs, which they use for hopping and jumping great distances. Wallabies are herbivores, feeding on grasses, vegetables, leaves, and other vegetation. They are capable of leaping distances of up to 3 meters in a single bound. Wallabies have a highly developed sense of smell and hearing, and their large feet act as shock absorbers during leaping. They are generally shy and will flee if approached too closely.

The Red-necked wallaby is a medium-sized macropod marsupial, common in eastern Australia from New South Wales to the Queensland border area, through to South Australia, and in Tasmania. There is also a large introduced population in New Zealand, and small colonies in Scotland, England, Ireland, and France. The Red Necked Wallaby is visually very similar to the Black Striped Wallaby, with their only difference being the lack of a black stripe, larger size and their namesake red neck.

The most common wallaby in North Australia, Agile wallabies inhabit dry open woodland, heaths, dunes and grassland and are often present in the vicinity of rivers and lakes. When grass is in short supply, they are sometimes known to move onto agricultural land, including sugar cane plantations. Agile wallabies are generally solitary animals, but they sometimes form into groups when feeding on open pastures. This behaviour may help with predator awareness.

The tammar wallaby, also known as the dama wallaby, is a small macropod native to South and Western Australia. Though its geographical range has been severely reduced since European colonisation, the tammar wallaby remains common within its reduced range. The tammar wallaby is among the smallest of the wallabies in their genus, and have several notable adaptations, including the ability to retain energy while hopping, colour vision, and the ability to drink seawater.

Albino wallabies are a rare and fascinating phenomenon, often found in captivity or on rare sightings in the wild. Generally a genetic mutation of the Red-Necked Wallaby, Albino wallabies are one of the most common mutations in the animal kingdom. Unfortunately, some wallabies are bred for these characteristics, creating issues with inbreeding and genetic deformities. In May 2025, an albino wallaby was found wandering the countryside of Kent, UK.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.dui: One of the most physically adapted small antelope, duikers have several adaptations to defend their young and home territory. For some species, this includes stripes that may reduce injury to the more vulnerable abdominal area and may also make them more difficult for some predators to identify by breaking up the outline of their form. When the duiker has been spotted by a predator, it will first freeze, and then bound away with the characteristic duiker diving motion into the safety of the thick brush.

The blue duiker is a small antelope found in central, southern and eastern Africa. It is the smallest duiker. The species was first described by Swedish naturalist Carl Peter Thunberg in 1789. 12 subspecies are identified. The blue duiker reaches 32–41 centimetres at the shoulder. Their dark tail measures slightly above 10 centimetres and they have short, spiky horns, (around 5 centimetres long) hidden in their hair tufts. The blue duiker bears a significant resemblance to Maxwell's duiker.

While the red forest duiker is very similar to the common duiker, it is smaller in size and has a distinguishing reddish coloring. Red forest duikers tend to roam singly, in pairs, or small family groups, and it is rare to see a group of more than three individuals.The cry of red forest duikers is rather distinctive, loud, and penetrating, sounding somewhere between a snort and a whistle.

The Red-flanked duiker is one of the smallest species of antelope. They have russet coats, with greyish-black legs and backs, and white underbellies. There are small white markings on the ears and snout and a dark streak runs along the center of the face. A tuft of black hairs grows between the horns and further coarse dark hairs grow along the top of the neck. Their legs are bluish-grey. The sexes are in general similar in appearance but males have short backward-pointing horns.

The Zebra duiker is a small antelope found in Africa. It is believed to be one of the earliest duiker species to have evolved. Zebra duikers have gold or red-brown coats with 12-16 distinctive zebra-like stripes, dark markings on their upper legs, and russet faces. Newborns appear darker because they are born with their stripes closer together. Their horns are short and round with sharp pointed tips.
informational_blurb.exhibitadditions.gue: Guenons are a group of medium-sized monkeys that have long back legs, a rounded head, a long tail that helps them balance while moving through the trees, and large cheek pouches. The word guenon comes from the French word for monkey. Monkeys in the guenon group are some of the most colorful, graceful, and lively in Africa. Guenons are best known for their striking color patterns, such as hip stripes, brow bands, or a white nose spot or band. Facial adornments can also include a throat ruff, beard, or mustache.

The DeBrazza’s Guenon is the largest species in the guenon family, it is one of the most widespread arboreal African primates. Aside from size, it can be differentiated from other guenons by its orange diadem and white beard. Due to its cryptic nature, the species is not well documented in all of its habitats but has shown unique traits such as pair-bonding and aggressive behavior towards other guenons. De Brazza's monkeys are social animals, forming very small groups of 4 - 10 individuals.

Red-tailed monkeys are named, surprisingly, for the red coloration of their tails. These monkeys have a white nose and cheeks in the midst of black or dark grey body fur. They also have very large, elastic cheeks which are used in gathering food and storing it in their mouths for safety. Red-tailed monkeys are social primates that form groups of 7-30 individuals. The groups consist of one dominant male and females and their offspring. Groups generally stay together throughout the day and through life.

Diana monkeys belong to the Old World monkey family. They are generally black or dark grey but have a white throat, crescent-shaped browband, ruff, and beard. The browband gave the species its common name since it was held to resemble the crescent on the brow of the goddess Diana. These monkeys have white underarms and a white stripe down their thighs. The backs of their thighs and their lower backs are a chestnut color. Apart from the beard and some fringes on their limbs, their fur is short and sleek in appearance.

The blue monkey or diademed monkey (Cercopithecus mitis ) is a species of Old World monkey native to Central and East Africa, ranging from the upper Congo River basin east to the East African Rift and south to northern Angola and Zambia.Despite what the common name suggests, the Blue monkey is not blue. In fact, the species is so called due to the hairless face, which seems to be colored in blue. This Old world monkey is of great interest to scientists. The primate has a dark head top.

Wolf's mona monkey is a colorful Old World monkey from central Africa. It was first described from a living specimen in the Zoological Garden at Dresden. It was bought in 1887 by Dr Ludwig Wolf from somewhere in central West Africa. The species was described in 1891 and named after the collector. The color of these monkeys is used in intraspecific communication for recognizing individuals, species, and potential mates. Wolf's mona monkey is dark grey with a red "saddle" on its back.
